description: Return leads (people) matching an ICP. Free by default while the account has free thin rows left today (a daily quota; detail "thin" guarantees $0). detail "full" is billable: about $0.02 per returned row (0 rows costs $0) at the Tier 0 list price. Accounts can pay a different rate: get_balance returns this account's prices, and every response reports what was actually spent in cost.amount_charged_usd. Realtime, and an automatic escalation to it, are billed per row too. count_leads sizes the audience for free first. Rows never include email or phone; generate_email (which takes the lead id) and find_phone add those for the ids you keep. Ordering is not stable, so pages are fetched by passing the ids you already have in exclude_ids rather than by offset.

allow_unlisted_values.description: Escape hatch. This server checks industry / seniority / headcount / company-type values against the LinkedIn vocabularies before sending, because the API silently returns 0 results for an unknown industry or seniority instead of rejecting it. Set true only when you are sure a value is valid and this server is out of date.

changed_jobs.description: Only leads who recently changed jobs — realtime only: using it forces the pricier live mode.

compact.description: Default true: return a small per-lead summary (including the Generect `id`, which every later step accepts). Set false for the full raw record (~80 fields) — only worth it when you specifically need skills, education or other deep fields.

company_filters.description: Optional: only return leads at companies matching these filters (two-level ICP).

allow_unlisted_values.description: Escape hatch for the local vocabulary check — see the lead-side field of the same name.

company_names.description: Restrict to specific company names — realtime only: using it forces the pricier live mode.

company_types.description: Company types: "Public Company","Privately Held","Non Profit","Government Agency","Educational", …

department_headcount.description: Department size, e.g. {"name":"engineering","min":10,"max":100} — realtime only: using it forces the pricier live mode.

exclude_domains.description: Exclude companies by domain (e.g. existing customers).

headcount_growth.description: Headcount growth in percent — realtime only: using it forces the pricier live mode.

hiring_on_linkedin.description: Only companies actively hiring — realtime only: using it forces the pricier live mode.

industries.description: Company industries. Must match Generect industry names exactly (e.g. "Software Development"); unknown names are rejected with HTTP 400.

keywords.description: Free-text keywords across name/description/specialties — realtime only: using it forces the pricier live mode.

linkedins_links.description: Specific LinkedIn company URLs — realtime only: using it forces the pricier live mode.

locations.description: HQ locations — cities, states or countries.

num_of_followers.description: LinkedIn follower buckets: "1-50","51-100","101-1000","1001-5000","5001+" — realtime only: using it forces the pricier live mode.

revenues_range.description: Annual revenue range, single object {min,max} — realtime only: using it forces the pricier live mode.

sub_industries.description: Expand each selected industry to its sub-industries as well (broadens the match).

technologies.description: Technologies the company uses — realtime only: using it forces the pricier live mode.

company_id.description: Anchor to one company by LinkedIn numeric id.

company_industries.description: Industry of the current employer. Must match Generect industry names exactly (e.g. "Software Development", "Financial Services"); names are hierarchical and unknown names are rejected with HTTP 400 naming the field.

company_link.description: Anchor to one company by LinkedIn URL.

company_locations.description: HQ location of the lead's current employer.

company_name.description: Anchor to one company by name (exclusive with company_link/company_id).

company_types.description: Employer types: "Public Company","Privately Held","Non Profit","Government Agency","Educational","Self Employed","Self Owned","Partnership".

confirm_spend_usd.description: Explicit approval for an unusually large charge. Calls whose worst case exceeds $5 are refused unless this is set to at least the amount the tool reports. Only set it after the user has agreed to that number.

detail.description: Row detail for the database search. Thin rows are FREE — id, name, job_title, seniority, location, company name/id/industry/country; no LinkedIn URL, domain, contacts or history — up to a daily per-account row quota that resets at 00:00 UTC. Omitted (default): thin while the free tier is available; once it is not (quota spent, a custom-contract account, a server without the tier) the search continues as before — full rows billed per row, marked thin_unavailable in the result, under the spend ceiling. "thin": free rows only — never billed, never escalated to realtime; a spent quota is a 429 and a realtime-only filter is an error. "full": the whole record, billed per row. Browse thin, then spend only on the rows you keep: generate_email takes the lead id directly, enrich_* gives the full record.

exclude_ids.description: Skip leads by Generect/Sales-Navigator id. Pass the ids you already received to paginate without duplicates — ordering is not stable, so this is more reliable than offset.

exclude_names.description: Skip leads by full name. Works in both modes (the database-mode bug that returned 0 rows was fixed in the API on 2026-08-13, PRO-1333). exclude_ids is still the more reliable way to paginate.

exclude_title_keywords.description: DEPRECATED — accepted but ignored. No v1 equivalent. Narrow job_titles instead, or filter the returned rows yourself.

filter_empty_vars.description: Drop leads where these fields are empty, e.g. ["profile_photo","job_started_on"]. Useful to raise data quality before paying.

functions.description: Job functions, e.g. ["Sales","Marketing","Engineering"] — realtime only: using it forces the pricier live mode.

get_max_leads.description: DEPRECATED — accepted but ignored. Always on now: search responses include results_count without asking.

job_title.description: DEPRECATED alias for job_titles. Still honoured: it is merged into job_titles.

job_titles.description: Target job titles, OR-matched (e.g. ["CEO","Founder","Owner"]). A lead needs to match only one.

keywords.description: Free-text keywords across headline/summary/skills — realtime only: using it forces the pricier live mode.

lead_industries.description: DEPRECATED — accepted but ignored. Removed: v1 filters on the employer's industry. Use company_industries.

limit_by.description: Rows to return this call (1–100, default 25). You are billed per returned row, so this number IS the price of the call.

linkedin_filter_link.description: A LinkedIn / Sales Navigator search URL to lift filters from — realtime only: using it forces the pricier live mode.

locations.description: Where the lead lives — matches cities, states and countries, e.g. ["United States","Berlin"].

mode.description: Data mode. "database" = Generect's own index: sub-second, free counts, free thin rows (see detail) or cheaper full rows; it accepts a subset of the filters today and names any it rejects. "realtime" = live LinkedIn lookup, 5–60s, billed per row, accepts every realtime filter. "auto" (default) tries database first and escalates to realtime only if a filter you passed is rejected there (the escalation is reported, and is refused above the per-call spend ceiling). Pick "database" explicitly when freshness is not critical and cost matters more than freshness.

past_company_names.description: Companies the lead previously worked at (alumni targeting) — realtime only: using it forces the pricier live mode.

personas.description: Advanced raw persona tuples [name, functions, seniorities, prohibits, priority?] — realtime only: using it forces the pricier live mode.

posted_on_linkedin.description: Only leads who recently posted on LinkedIn — realtime only: using it forces the pricier live mode.

seniorities.description: Seniority at the current employer, e.g. ["Owner","CXO","VP","Director","Manager"]. Current position only.

without_company.description: DEPRECATED — accepted but ignored. No longer needed — v1 filter-only search is the default when no company anchor is set.

years_in_company.description: Time at current company, same buckets as years_in_position — realtime only: using it forces the pricier live mode.

years_in_position.description: Time in current role: 1=<1y, 2=1-2y, 3=3-5y, 4=6-10y, 5=10y+ — realtime only: using it forces the pricier live mode.
